review.summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR defects found in the supplied scope. The three new webinar layouts use a single open_url button to `#webinar-registration`. The native form gets that exact static id, so the fragment target matches. Each variant uses the shared `signup` box once (hero columns for course, a signup section for workshop/strategy), so node ids are not duplicated. The section counts of 4/5/5 follow from the code (course omits the signup section), and there is exactly one h1 per template. The form change is a single added attribute with no handler, field or validation changes. Two low-confidence MINOR residual risks are listed below; both depend on page composition that is not included in the supplied text. Test and browser results were not verified here.

findings.area: Fragment target dependency and static id uniqueness
findings.issue: The CTA's `#webinar-registration` target exists only if the page also renders WebinarRegistrationForm. The form id is static, so it would be duplicated if a page renders more than one instance of this component.
findings.evidence: The templates contain only an open_url to `#webinar-registration`. The form hard-codes `id="webinar-registration"`. The supplied text does not show that the template is restricted to pages with exactly one webinar experience form.
findings.impact: If a gallery layout is inserted on a page or step without a bound webinar form, the CTA is a silent no-op. If a page ever renders two webinar forms, the HTML ids are duplicated and the jump goes to the first one. This is an edge case, since the stated design places the form on the same page.
findings.recommended_fix: Confirm that the webinar page or step always renders exactly one native form below these layouts. Optionally add `scroll-margin-top` to the form if there is a fixed header. Do not add a framework.
findings.required_test: Render a page containing one of the new layouts and the native webinar form. Assert exactly one element with id `webinar-registration` in the document. Optionally assert that the fragment link resolves to a form.
